q: Biology is the study of ____ things.
e: Biology is the study of living things. Living things are organisms: plants, animals, fungi, and microbes.

q: A large variety of living things exists on the land, in the water and in the ____.
e: A large variety of living things exists on the land, in the water and in the air. Air is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Living things (organisms) include plants, animals including ____ and other organisms.
e: Living things (organisms) include plants, animals including humans and other organisms. Humans is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Biology deals with the study of all organisms that live or have ever lived on the ____ .
e: Biology deals with the study of all organisms that live or have ever lived on the earth. Earth is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Biology is very fundamental and important science dealing with bacteria, protista, fungi, plants and ____ including humans.
e: Biology is very fundamental and important science dealing with bacteria, protista, fungi, plants and animals including humans. Animals is the idea that completes this fact.

q: To a great extent, we owe our daily high standard of living to biological advances in two areas: food production and ____ control.
e: To a great extent, we owe our daily high standard of living to biological advances in two areas: food production and disease control. Vaccines, antibiotics, and public-health biology all help control disease.

q: Plants and animals breeders have modified organisms to yield greater amounts of ____ than did older varieties.
e: Plants and animals breeders have modified organisms to yield greater amounts of food than did older varieties. Food is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Biological research has also improved food production by developing controls for the disease organisms, pests and ____ that reduce yields.
e: Biological research has also improved food production by developing controls for the disease organisms, pests and weeds that reduce yields. Weeds is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Biologists must understand the nature of these harmful organisms to develop effective ____ methods.
e: Biologists must understand the nature of these harmful organisms to develop effective control methods. Control is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The main branches of biology are: Botany: study of ____
e: The main branches of biology are: Botany: study of plants. Botany is the branch of biology that studies plants.

q: Zoology: study of ____
e: Zoology: study of animals. Zoology is the branch of biology that studies animals.

q: Microbiology: study of ____ organisms.
e: Microbiology: study of microscopic organisms. Microscopic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Morphology: study of forms and structures of ____
e: Morphology: study of forms and structures of organisms. Organisms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Anatomy: study of gross internal structures of ____
e: Anatomy: study of gross internal structures of organisms. Organisms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Histology: study of ____ structures of tissues.
e: Histology: study of microscopic structures of tissues. Microscopic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Cytology: study of ____
e: Cytology: study of cells. The cell is the basic unit of structure and function in living organisms.

q: Physiology: study of living processes or functions of the various parts of ____
e: Physiology: study of living processes or functions of the various parts of organisms. Organisms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Embryology: study of early development of ____
e: Embryology: study of early development of organisms. Organisms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Palaeontology: study of ____ (the remains of organisms that lived millions of years ago; now preserved in rocks).
e: Palaeontology: study of fossils (the remains of organisms that lived millions of years ago; now preserved in rocks). Fossils is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Ecology: study of the relationships of organisms to their ____
e: Ecology: study of the relationships of organisms to their environments. Environments is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Biodiversity: study of varieties among living ____
e: Biodiversity: study of varieties among living organisms. Organisms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Evolution: study of the origin and change in forms of organisms over ____
e: Evolution: study of the origin and change in forms of organisms over time. Time is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Genetics: study of heredity and ____
e: Genetics: study of heredity and variations. Variations is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Mycology: study of ____
e: Mycology: study of fungi. Fungi is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Protistology: study of ____
e: Protistology: study of protists. Protists are mostly eukaryotic and can be uni- or multicellular, auto- or heterotrophic.

q: Phycology: study of ____
e: Phycology: study of algae. Algae is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Virology: study of ____
e: Virology: study of viruses. Viruses is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bacteriology: study of ____
e: Bacteriology: study of bacteria. Bacteria is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Molecular Biology: study of ____ in organisms.
e: Molecular Biology: study of molecules in organisms. Molecules is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Biotechnology: study of utilization of living organisms in ____ processes.
e: Biotechnology: study of utilization of living organisms in industrial processes. Industrial is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bioinformatics: study of information technology to interpret molecular biology ____
e: Bioinformatics: study of information technology to interpret molecular biology data. Data is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The main characteristics of living things are their cellular structure, metabolism, growth, movement, irritability, reproduction and ____ .
e: The main characteristics of living things are their cellular structure, metabolism, growth, movement, irritability, reproduction and adaptability. Adaptability helps a species survive when conditions change.

q: All living things consist of the living substance called ____ which forms the basis of cells.
e: All living things consist of the living substance called protoplasm which forms the basis of cells. Protoplasm is the living material of a cell, including cytoplasm and the nucleus.

q: These cells contain ____ molecules that carry biological information.
e: These cells contain DNA molecules that carry biological information. DNA carries the genetic information that cells use to build and run an organism.

q: Cells of plants and animals are organized into ____ and tissues are in turn organized into organs and systems.
e: Cells of plants and animals are organized into tissues and tissues are in turn organized into organs and systems. A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together. An organ is made of tissues that combine to do a job, such as the heart or a leaf.

q: Metabolism is the sum of the various processes that give the organism’s ____ .
e: Metabolism is the sum of the various processes that give the organism’s life. Life is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The two aspects of metabolism are ____ and catabolism.
e: The two aspects of metabolism are anabolism and catabolism. Metabolism is anabolism plus catabolism: build-up and break-down reactions in a body. Anabolism builds larger molecules and usually needs energy.

q: The food material is made into a part of the organism in the process of ____ .
e: The food material is made into a part of the organism in the process of anabolism. Anabolism builds larger molecules and usually needs energy.

q: The food material, when broken down, releases energy and results in the formation of ____ products.
e: The food material, when broken down, releases energy and results in the formation of waste products. Waste is the idea that completes this fact.

q: This process is termed as ____ .
e: This process is termed as catabolism. Catabolism breaks molecules down and can release energy.

q: The important metabolic processes that take place in organisms involve the utilization of ____ .
e: The important metabolic processes that take place in organisms involve the utilization of food. Food is the idea that completes this fact.

q: This includes nutrition, respiration and ____ .
e: This includes nutrition, respiration and excretion. Excretion is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The growth of an organism is seen as an increase in size and weight resulting from the use of ____ to further develop structures in the organism.
e: The growth of an organism is seen as an increase in size and weight resulting from the use of food to further develop structures in the organism. Food is the idea that completes this fact.

q: All living things show some kinds of ____ .
e: All living things show some kinds of movement. Movement is the idea that completes this fact.

q: This is more obvious in animals since they have organs of movement or ____ .
e: This is more obvious in animals since they have organs of movement or locomotion. Locomotion is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Movements in plants mainly take place inside the cells although some results from a stimulus such as ____ .
e: Movements in plants mainly take place inside the cells although some results from a stimulus such as light. Light is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Living things respond to ____ .
e: Living things respond to stimulus. A stimulus is a change in the surroundings that an organism can detect.

q: The stimulus can be any changes in the environment (light, sound, touch, temperature, etc.) which brings about a reaction in an organism due to a sensitivity to the ____ .
e: The stimulus can be any changes in the environment (light, sound, touch, temperature, etc.) which brings about a reaction in an organism due to a sensitivity to the stimulus. A stimulus is a change in the surroundings that an organism can detect.

q: Reproduction is the production of a new generation of ____ .
e: Reproduction is the production of a new generation of organisms. Organisms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The two types of reproduction are asexual reproduction and ____ reproduction.
e: The two types of reproduction are asexual reproduction and sexual reproduction. Sexual reproduction joins gametes from two parents and mixes genes.

q: In asexual reproduction, the new individual may be produced by a part of the ____ one.
e: In asexual reproduction, the new individual may be produced by a part of the old one. Old is the idea that completes this fact.

q: There is only one parent organism needed for ____ reproduction.
e: There is only one parent organism needed for asexual reproduction. Asexual reproduction makes offspring from one parent without gametes fusing.

q: Sexual reproduction produces a new individual as a result of the fusion of two parental ____ cells.
e: Sexual reproduction produces a new individual as a result of the fusion of two parental sex cells. Sex is the idea that completes this fact.

q: These two cells come, one from each individual of the same ____ .
e: These two cells come, one from each individual of the same species. Species is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Living organisms are able to adjust and adapt themselves to changes in their external and ____ environments.
e: Living organisms are able to adjust and adapt themselves to changes in their external and internal environments. Internal is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Adaptability increases the chances of species surviving and can result in the formation of a new ____ .
e: Adaptability increases the chances of species surviving and can result in the formation of a new species. Species is the idea that completes this fact.

q: For instance, a change of seasons or a shortage of food may cause certain birds to migrate to another place where the conditions are more ____ .
e: For instance, a change of seasons or a shortage of food may cause certain birds to migrate to another place where the conditions are more favourable. Favourable is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A plant may grow very straight and upright to stand above plants around it. This enables this plant or plant species to get enough ____ to survive and even to dominate the environment.
e: A plant may grow very straight and upright to stand above plants around it. This enables this plant or plant species to get enough sunlight to survive and even to dominate the environment. Sunlight is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The science of classification of organisms is called ____ .
e: The science of classification of organisms is called taxonomy. Taxonomy sorts living things into ranked groups so millions of species can be studied.

q: This is the general name for groups or categories within a classification system.
e: Taxa is the missing word. Taxa is the idea that completes this fact.

q: There are vast numbers of living things in the world. The word ‘biodiversity’ is a short form of ‘____ diversity’.
e: There are vast numbers of living things in the world. The word ‘biodiversity’ is a short form of ‘biological diversity’. Biological is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Scientists are not aware just how many different types of organisms exist in nature. It is because, previously unknown species are being ____ all the time.
e: Scientists are not aware just how many different types of organisms exist in nature. It is because, previously unknown species are being discovered all the time. Discovered is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Classification is essential to biology because there are too many different living things to sort out and compare unless they are organized into manageable ____ .
e: Classification is essential to biology because there are too many different living things to sort out and compare unless they are organized into manageable categories. Categories is the idea that completes this fact.

q: With an effective classification system in use, it is easier to organize the ideas about organisms and make ____ .
e: With an effective classification system in use, it is easier to organize the ideas about organisms and make generalizations. Generalizations is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The scheme of classification has to be ____ , allowing newly discovered living organisms to be added into the scheme where they fit best.
e: The scheme of classification has to be flexible, allowing newly discovered living organisms to be added into the scheme where they fit best. Flexible is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Just as similar species are grouped together into the same ____ .
e: Just as similar species are grouped together into the same genus. Genus is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Similar genera are grouped together into ____ .
e: Similar genera are grouped together into families. Families is the idea that completes this fact.

q: This approach is extended from families to orders, then classes, phyla or divisions and ____ .
e: This approach is extended from families to orders, then classes, phyla or divisions and kingdoms. Kingdoms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: By taxonomy, it is much easier to learn biology as there are millions of known and unknown ____ .
e: By taxonomy, it is much easier to learn biology as there are millions of known and unknown organisms. Organisms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Taxonomy can be used to examine the evolutionary history of organisms and the relationships between ____ .
e: Taxonomy can be used to examine the evolutionary history of organisms and the relationships between organisms. Organisms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The process of classification involves giving every organism an agreed ____ .
e: The process of classification involves giving every organism an agreed name. Classification groups organisms by shared features so we can name and compare them.

q: Placing the organism into a group based on the common characteristics it shares with others in the ____ .
e: Placing the organism into a group based on the common characteristics it shares with others in the group. Group is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The classification of organisms is essential to biology because it helps scientists to understand the ____ of life.
e: The classification of organisms is essential to biology because it helps scientists to understand the diversity of life. Diversity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The importance of taxonomy lies in its ability to organize and categorize the vast number of ____ in nature.
e: The importance of taxonomy lies in its ability to organize and categorize the vast number of species in nature. Species is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Taxonomic hierarchy helps in establishing the relationship among different ____ .
e: Taxonomic hierarchy helps in establishing the relationship among different organisms. Organisms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The classification system allows scientists to communicate about organisms in a clear and ____ manner.
e: The classification system allows scientists to communicate about organisms in a clear and consistent manner. Consistent is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Taxonomy is fundamental for understanding the biological ____ of organisms.
e: Taxonomy is fundamental for understanding the biological relationships of organisms. Relationships is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The taxonomic classification system is based on shared ____ among organisms.
e: The taxonomic classification system is based on shared characteristics among organisms. Characteristics is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The hierarchical structure of classification includes ranks such as kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, and ____ .
e: The hierarchical structure of classification includes ranks such as kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, and species. Species is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The classification of organisms is based on their evolutionary ____ .
e: The classification of organisms is based on their evolutionary history. History is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Taxonomy provides a framework for understanding the evolutionary ____ of organisms.
e: Taxonomy provides a framework for understanding the evolutionary relationships of organisms. Relationships is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The classification system is essential for organizing the vast diversity of ____ in the natural world.
e: The classification system is essential for organizing the vast diversity of life in the natural world. Life is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Taxonomy helps in identifying and describing new ____ as they are discovered.
e: Taxonomy helps in identifying and describing new species as they are discovered. Taxonomy sorts living things into ranked groups so millions of species can be studied.

q: The hierarchical classification system allows scientists to categorize organisms based on their shared ____ .
e: The hierarchical classification system allows scientists to categorize organisms based on their shared traits. Traits is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The classification of organisms is essential for understanding their ecological ____ .
e: The classification of organisms is essential for understanding their ecological roles. Roles is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Taxonomy aids in the study of the evolutionary relationships among different ____ .
e: Taxonomy aids in the study of the evolutionary relationships among different species. Species is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The classification system allows scientists to communicate about organisms in a clear and ____ manner.
e: The classification system allows scientists to communicate about organisms in a clear and consistent manner. Consistent is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Taxonomy is fundamental for understanding the biological ____ of organisms.
e: Taxonomy is fundamental for understanding the biological relationships of organisms. Relationships is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The taxonomic classification system is based on shared ____ among organisms.
e: The taxonomic classification system is based on shared characteristics among organisms. Characteristics is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The hierarchical structure of classification includes ranks such as kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, and ____ .
e: The hierarchical structure of classification includes ranks such as kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, and species. Species is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The classification of organisms is based on their evolutionary ____ .
e: The classification of organisms is based on their evolutionary history. History is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Taxonomy provides a framework for understanding the evolutionary ____ of organisms.
e: Taxonomy provides a framework for understanding the evolutionary relationships of organisms. Relationships is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The classification system is essential for organizing the vast diversity of ____ in the natural world.
e: The classification system is essential for organizing the vast diversity of life in the natural world. Life is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Taxonomy helps in identifying and describing new ____ as they are discovered.
e: Taxonomy helps in identifying and describing new species as they are discovered. Taxonomy sorts living things into ranked groups so millions of species can be studied.

q: The hierarchical classification system allows scientists to categorize organisms based on their shared ____ .
e: The hierarchical classification system allows scientists to categorize organisms based on their shared traits. Traits is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The classification of organisms is essential for understanding their ecological ____ .
e: The classification of organisms is essential for understanding their ecological roles. Roles is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Taxonomy aids in the study of the evolutionary relationships among different ____ .
e: Taxonomy aids in the study of the evolutionary relationships among different species. Species is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A Kingdom is a subdivision of a ____ .
e: A Kingdom is a subdivision of a Domain. Domains sit above kingdoms: Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya.

q: The living things are classified and placed in one of the six ____ .
e: The living things are classified and placed in one of the six kingdoms. A common six-kingdom set is Eubacteria, Archaebacteria, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.

q: The three domains - Bacteria, Archaea and ____ diverged early in the history of life.
e: The three domains - Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya diverged early in the history of life. Eukarya is the domain of organisms with nucleated cells. Domains sit above kingdoms: Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya.

q: Subsequently, many new kinds of organisms have ____ .
e: Subsequently, many new kinds of organisms have evolved. Evolved is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Each of these kingdoms has its own set of ____ .
e: Each of these kingdoms has its own set of characteristics. Characteristics is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Organisms are divided into six kingdoms. There are two kingdoms within the domains Archaea and Bacteria, namely kingdoms ____ and Eubacteria.
e: Organisms are divided into six kingdoms. There are two kingdoms within the domains Archaea and Bacteria, namely kingdoms Archaebacteria and Eubacteria. Archaebacteria is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Their differences are based primarily on the metabolism and ____ composition of the organisms.
e: Their differences are based primarily on the metabolism and genetic composition of the organisms. Genetic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Within the domain Eukarya, there are four kingdoms: Protista, Fungi, Plantae and ____ .
e: Within the domain Eukarya, there are four kingdoms: Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia. Animalia covers multicellular heterotrophs that usually move and lack cell walls.

q: The characteristics of six kingdoms include factors such as cellular structure, reproduction, and ____ .
e: The characteristics of six kingdoms include factors such as cellular structure, reproduction, and metabolism. Metabolism is the sum of chemical processes that keep an organism alive.

q: The kingdom Protista contains unicellular and ____ groups.
e: The kingdom Protista contains unicellular and colonial groups. Colonial is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The term protist means 'any eukaryotic organism that is not a ____ , animal or fungus'.
e: The term protist means 'any eukaryotic organism that is not a plant, animal or fungus'. Plant is the idea that completes this fact.

q: About 60,000 protist species have been described. They are the most ____ of the four kingdoms in the domain Eukarya.
e: About 60,000 protist species have been described. They are the most diverse of the four kingdoms in the domain Eukarya. Diverse is the idea that completes this fact.

q: They live in water, but a few species live in ____ areas.
e: They live in water, but a few species live in moist areas. Moist is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Some can even live in the human ____ .
e: Some can even live in the human intestine. Intestine is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Nucleus and other organelles are present in protists, allowing for complex cellular ____ .
e: Nucleus and other organelles are present in protists, allowing for complex cellular functions. Functions is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Movement is often by flagella, cilia, or ____ .
e: Movement is often by flagella, cilia, or pseudopodia. Pseudopodia is the idea that completes this fact.

q: They reproduce asexually by fission, budding or ____ .
e: They reproduce asexually by fission, budding or fragmentation. Fragmentation is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Most protists can be divided into three main groups based on their characteristics: Plant-like protists, Animal-like protists, and ____ -like protists.
e: Most protists can be divided into three main groups based on their characteristics: Plant-like protists, Animal-like protists, and Fungus -like protists. Fungus is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Plant-like protists contain chlorophyll in chloroplasts and make their own ____ .
e: Plant-like protists contain chlorophyll in chloroplasts and make their own food. Food is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Animal-like protists have no chlorophyll, feed on other organisms and can move from place to place (e.g., ____ ).
e: Animal-like protists have no chlorophyll, feed on other organisms and can move from place to place (e.g., Amoeba). Amoeba is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fungus-like protists lack chlorophyll, feed on dead organic matter and lack ____ in their cell walls.
e: Fungus-like protists lack chlorophyll, feed on dead organic matter and lack chitin in their cell walls. Fungal cell walls are made of chitin.

q: The protists include six general groups according to the characteristics: Chlorophyta, Euglenophyta, Chrysophyta, Rhizopoda, Actinopoda, and ____ .
e: The protists include six general groups according to the characteristics: Chlorophyta, Euglenophyta, Chrysophyta, Rhizopoda, Actinopoda, and Foraminifera. Foraminifera is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chlorophyta are photosynthetic, unicellular, without flagella, and contain ____ .
e: Chlorophyta are photosynthetic, unicellular, without flagella, and contain chlorophyll. Chlorophyll is the green pigment that captures light energy in plants.

q: Euglenophyta are some photosynthetic, others heterotrophic, unicellular, and contain chlorophylls or ____ .
e: Euglenophyta are some photosynthetic, others heterotrophic, unicellular, and contain chlorophylls or none. None is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Heterotrophic protists include groups like Chrysophyta, which are unicellular and manufacture the carbohydrate ____ .
e: Heterotrophic protists include groups like Chrysophyta, which are unicellular and manufacture the carbohydrate chrysolaminarin. Chrysolaminarin is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Rhizopoda move by pseudopodia and reproduce asexually by binary ____ .
e: Rhizopoda move by pseudopodia and reproduce asexually by binary fission. Binary fission is how many bacteria split into two similar cells.

q: Actinopoda have glassy skeletons and needle-like ____ .
e: Actinopoda have glassy skeletons and needle-like pseudopods. Pseudopods is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Foraminifera have rigid shells and move by protoplasmic ____ .
e: Foraminifera have rigid shells and move by protoplasmic streaming. Streaming is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fungi are eukaryotic organisms that are heterotrophic and reproduce by means of ____ .
e: Fungi are eukaryotic organisms that are heterotrophic and reproduce by means of spores. Spores is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A collection of hyphae, thin thread-like filaments form the ____ .
e: A collection of hyphae, thin thread-like filaments form the mycelia. Mycelia is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chlorophyll is absent in fungi, making them unable to carry out ____ .
e: Chlorophyll is absent in fungi, making them unable to carry out photosynthesis. Photosynthesis uses chlorophyll to trap light and build sugar from carbon dioxide and water.

q: Fungi grow as parasites on other organisms or as saprophytes on decaying organic matter in the ____ .
e: Fungi grow as parasites on other organisms or as saprophytes on decaying organic matter in the soil. Soil is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The cell wall of hypha is made up of ____ .
e: The cell wall of hypha is made up of chitin. Fungal cell walls are made of chitin.

q: They reproduce in a variety of ways: vegetatively, asexually or ____ .
e: They reproduce in a variety of ways: vegetatively, asexually or sexually. Sexually is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The fungi are subdivided into five divisions: Chytridiomycota, Zygomycota, Ascomycota, Basidiomycota and ____ .
e: The fungi are subdivided into five divisions: Chytridiomycota, Zygomycota, Ascomycota, Basidiomycota and Deuteromycota. Deuteromycota is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chytridiomycota are the simplest and most primitive form of fungi, characterized by coenocytic hyphae and ____ reproduction.
e: Chytridiomycota are the simplest and most primitive form of fungi, characterized by coenocytic hyphae and sexual reproduction. Sexual reproduction joins gametes from two parents and mixes genes.

q: Zygomycota are conjugated fungi with aseptate hyphae and many ____ .
e: Zygomycota are conjugated fungi with aseptate hyphae and many nuclei. Nuclei is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Ascomycota, known as sac fungi, have septate and branched hyphae, and mostly reproduce by ____ .
e: Ascomycota, known as sac fungi, have septate and branched hyphae, and mostly reproduce by budding. In budding, a small outgrowth of the parent detaches and becomes a new individual.

q: Basidiomycota are club fungi that have club-shaped fruiting bodies called ____ .
e: Basidiomycota are club fungi that have club-shaped fruiting bodies called basidia. Basidia is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Deuteromycota are imperfect fungi that reproduce strictly by means of ____ .
e: Deuteromycota are imperfect fungi that reproduce strictly by means of conidia. Conidia is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Plants are eukaryotic and chlorophyll-containing organisms that obtain their energy from the sun through ____ .
e: Plants are eukaryotic and chlorophyll-containing organisms that obtain their energy from the sun through photosynthesis. Photosynthesis uses chlorophyll to trap light and build sugar from carbon dioxide and water.

q: The cell wall of plants is composed of ____ .
e: The cell wall of plants is composed of cellulose. Plant cell walls are made of cellulose.

q: Plants reproduce by vegetative, asexual and ____ methods.
e: Plants reproduce by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods. Sexual is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In the life cycle of plants, interchanges occur from the embryo and are supported by other ____ .
e: In the life cycle of plants, interchanges occur from the embryo and are supported by other tissues. A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together.

q: Plants lack ____ .
e: Plants lack motility. Motility is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The plantae are subdivided into five divisions: Thallophyta, Bryophyta, Pteridophyta, Gymnospermae and ____ .
e: The plantae are subdivided into five divisions: Thallophyta, Bryophyta, Pteridophyta, Gymnospermae and Angiospermae. Angiospermae is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Thallophyta have a simple plant body (thallus) and grow in water, on damp soil, on wet rocks and on ____ trunks.
e: Thallophyta have a simple plant body (thallus) and grow in water, on damp soil, on wet rocks and on tree trunks. Tree is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bryophyta are the most primitive land plants that grow on damp and ____ soil.
e: Bryophyta are the most primitive land plants that grow on damp and shaded soil. Shaded is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The life cycle of bryophytes shows two distinct generations (gametophytic and sporophytic generations), which regularly alternate with each other in a single life cycle, is called ____ of generations.
e: The life cycle of bryophytes shows two distinct generations (gametophytic and sporophytic generations), which regularly alternate with each other in a single life cycle, is called alternation of generations. Alternation is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Pteridophyta are more advanced than bryophytes and have a well-developed ____ system.
e: Pteridophyta are more advanced than bryophytes and have a well-developed vascular system. Vascular is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Gymnospermae are seed-bearing vascular plants with seeds that are not enclosed in a ____ .
e: Gymnospermae are seed-bearing vascular plants with seeds that are not enclosed in a fruit. Fruit is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Angiospermae are flowering vascular plants that produce seeds inside the ____ of the flower.
e: Angiospermae are flowering vascular plants that produce seeds inside the ovary of the flower. Ovary is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Animals are multicellular and ____ organisms.
e: Animals are multicellular and heterotrophic organisms. Heterotrophs must take in food made by other organisms.

q: Animals are divided into two main groups: those that do not have a backbone are grouped as ____ and those that have a backbone are grouped as vertebrates.
e: Animals are divided into two main groups: those that do not have a backbone are grouped as invertebrates and those that have a backbone are grouped as vertebrates. Invertebrates is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Invertebrates make up more than ____ percent of all animal species alive today.
e: Invertebrates make up more than 95 percent of all animal species alive today. 95 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Porifera are asymmetrical, pore-filter feeders, and are not motile (____).
e: Porifera are asymmetrical, pore-filter feeders, and are not motile (sessile). Sessile is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Cnidaria exhibit radial symmetry and have two cell layers only; ectoderm and endoderm with mesoglea between them, and all have ____ cells.
e: Cnidaria exhibit radial symmetry and have two cell layers only; ectoderm and endoderm with mesoglea between them, and all have stinging cells. Stinging is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Platyhelminthes have bilateral symmetry, cephalization with head and brain, and an incomplete ____ system.
e: Platyhelminthes have bilateral symmetry, cephalization with head and brain, and an incomplete digestive system. Digestive is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Nematoda are bilateral, have a complete digestive system with separate mouth and anus, and many are ____ .
e: Nematoda are bilateral, have a complete digestive system with separate mouth and anus, and many are parasitic. Parasitic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Annelida are segmented, have a true coelom, and include organisms like ____ and leeches.
e: Annelida are segmented, have a true coelom, and include organisms like earthworms and leeches. Earthworms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Mollusca have soft bodies, and some may have shells, including organisms like snails and ____ .
e: Mollusca have soft bodies, and some may have shells, including organisms like snails and octopuses. Octopuses is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Arthropoda have bilateral symmetry with jointed appendages and an ____ present.
e: Arthropoda have bilateral symmetry with jointed appendages and an exoskeleton present. Exoskeleton is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Echinodermata exhibit bilateral symmetry in embryo and radial symmetry in adult forms, with a water vascular system and ____ present on arms.
e: Echinodermata exhibit bilateral symmetry in embryo and radial symmetry in adult forms, with a water vascular system and tube feet present on arms. Tube feet is the idea that completes this fact.

q: All chordates have bilateral symmetry with three cell layers and a dorsal hollow nerve cord, along with a notochord, pharyngeal gill slits and ____ in embryo or adults.
e: All chordates have bilateral symmetry with three cell layers and a dorsal hollow nerve cord, along with a notochord, pharyngeal gill slits and tail in embryo or adults. Tail is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fish are vertebrates with scaly skin, live in water, and have ____ for swimming.
e: Fish are vertebrates with scaly skin, live in water, and have fins for swimming. Fins is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Amphibians have moist, scaleless skin, lay eggs in water, and undergo ____ from larva to adult.
e: Amphibians have moist, scaleless skin, lay eggs in water, and undergo metamorphosis from larva to adult. Metamorphosis is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Reptiles have scaly skin, lungs, and lay eggs with ____ .
e: Reptiles have scaly skin, lungs, and lay eggs with shells. Shells is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Birds have feathers, wings for flight, and are ____ thermic.
e: Birds have feathers, wings for flight, and are homoiothermic thermic. Homoiothermic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Mammals have hair, lungs, and young that feed on milk from ____ glands.
e: Mammals have hair, lungs, and young that feed on milk from mammary glands. Mammary is the idea that completes this fact.
